title: Financial Crime and the Board
summary: Plain-language grounding in the financial crime risks a firm faces, the international standards behind them and why supervisors hold the board accountable for the firm's defences.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: Plain-language grounding in the financial crime risks a firm faces, the international standards behind them and why supervisors hold the board accountable for the firm's defences.
Learning Objectives: Explain money laundering, terrorist and proliferation financing, sanctions evasion, fraud, bribery and tax evasion
Identify the international standards that shape national requirements
Define the board's responsibilities and distinguish them from management's
Syllabus: The financial crime landscape and how criminals exploit financial firms
FATF Recommendations, mutual evaluations and the risk-based approach
Board accountability and senior executive responsibility for financial crime
Intended Audience: Chairs, non-executive and independent directors and board committee members, especially on risk and audit committees
Executive directors and senior managers accountable for financial crime, compliance and operations
Company secretaries and heads of governance supporting board oversight
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Board or senior management experience in financial services is helpful. No specialist background in financial crime compliance is required.
Core Reading: FATF, International Standards on Combating Money Laundering and the Financing of Terrorism and Proliferation: The FATF Recommendations (as updated)
Basel Committee, Corporate Governance Principles for Banks (2015)
